hypotheses.reasoning: ingest-api heap was normal (young GC pauses, heap 30-48%) through about 17:00. At 17:01:14 (#531) it began reporting old-gen memory not reclaimed after full GC, with GC overhead 20%. That rose to 87% and 35% GC overhead at 17:04:39 (#783). Heap then ran out (#949 OutOfMemoryError in worker-4), and the container was OOMKilled (#950 for ingest-api-2, #1090 for ingest-api-0, 2Gi limit). The FATAL at #1089 points at eventCache.put, so the growing cache looks like the retained memory. While ingest-api restarts and re-warms its cache, the gateway has no healthy upstream and returns 502s (#981, and later #1190, #1342, #1433). The 502s are the symptom of the crashing pod, not the origin. No deploy or config event precedes the heap growth (the only version line is the restart at #973). The analytics-forwarder 429s from analytics-ingest (#391 onward) are a separate downstream rate limit and do not explain the ingest-api memory growth.

ingest-api is running v3.4.1 and restarts warm the event cache on startup, so a v3.4.1 defect in cache retention is possible. Nothing in the logs shows a rollout near 17:00, though, so this is weaker than the memory-growth reading.

verdict.recommendedAction: Treat ingest-api memory as the fix target. Capture a heap dump or check eventCache size and eviction on ingest-api v3.4.1 to confirm the leak, and add an eviction bound or a higher memory limit as a stopgap. Roll back to the prior build if the leak is confirmed as a v3.4.1 regression. Consider a gateway retry or circuit-breaker change so restarts don't surface as 502s. Separately, review analytics-forwarder's 429 handling (batches dropped after 5 attempts) and the analytics-ingest rate limit.
